'''Tsurugi Shrine''' (剱神社) often written as "剣神社," is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Kokubu-Shikine|ja|国分敷根|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubu Shikine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11420538}}, {{ill|Kirishima, Kagoshima|en|Kirishima, Kagoshima|qid=Q858352|lt=Kirishima, Kagoshima}}, {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|qid=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima Prefecture}}.

== Deities Enshrined ==
The principal deity is {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}}. Additionally, the shrine enshrines {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋根命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qid=Q2564508}}, "Tsurugihiko no Kami" (剱彦神), {{ill|Ōusu-no-Mikoto|ja|大碓皇子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oōusunomiko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11438297}}, "Kosunomiko" (小臼命, identified with Yamato Takeru), {{ill|Futodama|ja|太玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futodama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ}}, and {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}}. These deities were enshrined through amalgamation in 1910 (Meiji 43).

== History ==
Originally, the shrine was located atop Tsurugi Rock (剱岩), referred to as "Biwanku" (琵琶甲 or 枇琶甲), with a stone sanctuary at the summit and a worship hall at the base. In December 1674 (Enpō 1), it was relocated to its current site. The name "Tsurugi" derives from a legend where Yamato Takeru climbed the rock while scouting the {{ill|Kumaso|en|Kumaso|qid=Q1196897|lt=Kumaso}} during his conquest, resting with his sword.

During the reign of the Shikine clan, the shrine fell into neglect as they venerated {{ill|Tenmangū|en|Tenmangū|qid=Q798838|lt=Tenmangu}} as their ancestral shrine. It was later restored by {{ill|Shimazu Yoshihisa|en|Shimazu Yoshihisa|qid=Q955727|lt=Shimazu Yoshihisa}} under the order of {{ill|Yamada Toshiyasu|ja|山田利安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Toshiyasu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Records of this restoration exist in the "Shrine Registry" and "Tsurugi Shrine History" preserved by the Saruwatari family of Shikine.

On October 25, 1910, the shrine amalgamated with Hyōsu Shrine, Sugawara Shrine, Futodama Shrine, and Hiruko Shrine.

== Festivals and Rituals ==
The annual "Shinkōsai" (神幸祭) or "Mikoshi Procession" originates from a historical event where a summer epidemic was halted after a purification ritual performed by the shrine. The festival is now held to pray for health and protection against epidemics.

Additionally, monthly rituals are conducted on the 1st and 15th at 6 AM.

== Amalgamated Shrines ==
;Hyōsu Shrine
: Deity and origin unknown. Previously located in Hamaji Setta, Shikine Village, with a tiled main hall and a dance hall.

;Sugawara Shrine
: Dedicated to {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}}. Originally located in Setta, Shikine Village. Historical records mention its reconstruction in 1602 (Keichō 7) by Lord Yoshihisa Shimazu.

;Futodama Shrine
: Dedicated to {{ill|Futodama|ja|太玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futodama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ}}. Details unknown. Originally had a tiled main hall, dance hall, and bridge hall.

;Hiruko Shrine
: Dedicated to {{ill|Hiruko|ja|蛭子命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiruko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1067028|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1067028}}. Once featured a stone sanctuary in Setta, Shikine Village.
